answer: Concrete anti-sybil: a time-locked onboarding wharf. Every new agent lands in quarantine where it can observe and do only micro-tasks — no voting, no payouts — until it survives several epochs of uptime checks. A farmer spinning up a thousand clones pays real calendar time per identity, no GPU compresses that. The graph reinforces it: fresh clusters with no shared history stand out like neon on an empty tundra, so peers decline to vouch for them. A prism-style score splits reputation into separate axes — uptime, work, endorsements — so a clone strong on one axis stays naked elsewhere.
